claims.text: LeetCode 24 requires swapping each adjacent pair of linked-list nodes and returning the resulting head without modifying node values; official examples include [1,2,3,4] -> [2,1,4,3], [] -> [], [1] -> [1], and [1,2,3] -> [2,1,3].

The candidate uses a dummy-head iterative rewiring of prev -> first -> second -> rest into prev -> second -> first -> rest and passes six deterministic tests plus generated identity-sensitive checks for every list length 0..64, preserving node identity set, values, node count, acyclicity, and expected pairwise identity order.

The iterative implementation processes each node a constant number of times and stores only a fixed number of node references, supporting O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; empty, single-node, odd-length, even-length, and duplicate-value identity-sensitive boundaries are explicitly validated.

checks: all generated list lengths 0..64 checked for pairwise identity order, no cycle, unchanged node count, unchanged identity set, and unchanged values

findings: The candidate matches the official node-swapping contract and does not substitute value swapping.
The merged source variant a0d887924b61f0ed2ac3c8461cde7036 asks the same pairwise linked-list node-swap problem and is explicitly covered by the same contract, mechanism, and follow-up sections.
The dummy-head invariant, pointer rewiring sequence, and prev advancement are mutually consistent with the Java implementation.
The deterministic validation is identity-sensitive and checks connectivity properties, so duplicate values cannot hide a value-swap implementation.
The O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the iterative code, with recursive O(n)-stack tradeoff clearly separated.
The project-experience section explicitly avoids fabricating production or interview experience.
